record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Classify all finite connected 3-regular graphs G for which the standard round 3-sphere S^3 admits a connected embedded closed geodesic net modelled on G; equivalently, determine exactly which such G can be realized by an embedding into S^3 whose edges are distinct non-constant geodesic arcs, with no self-intersections or edge crossings except at common endpoints, and such that at every vertex the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors of the three incident edges is zero.

evidence.quote: A geodesic net on M consists of a finite set V of points of M (called vertices) that includes S and a finite set E of non-constant distinct geodesics between vertices (called edges)
Problem 2.0.2. Classify all 3-regular graphs G such that the round 3-sphere has a geodesic net modelled on G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ denote the unit round $3$-sphere with its standard Riemannian metric. A geodesic net on $S^3$ is a pair $(V,E)$ consisting of a finite set $V$ of points of $S^3$ (vertices) and a finite set $E$ of non-constant, pairwise distinct geodesic arcs (edges), each joining two vertices in $V$, such that at every vertex $v \in V$ the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors of all edges incident to $v$ equals $0 \in T_v S^3$. The geodesic net is called embedded if no edge has a self-intersection and any two distinct edges meet only at common endpoints in $V$; it is called connected if the underlying graph is connected.

Given a finite connected $3$-regular (i.e., every vertex has degree exactly $3$) graph $G$, we say that $S^3$ admits a closed embedded geodesic net modelled on $G$ if there exists an embedded geodesic net $(V,E)$ on $S^3$ whose underlying graph is isomorphic to $G$.

Problem: Determine, with proof, exactly which finite connected $3$-regular graphs $G$ have the property that $S^3$ admits a connected embedded closed geodesic net modelled on $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication appears to provide a full classification of 3-regular graphs realizable as embedded geodesic nets on the round 3-sphere. Related results exist for the round 2-sphere (Heppes-style classifications) and for flat surfaces, but the 3-sphere classification problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets on flat spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Classifications of 3-regular geodesic nets are discussed on 2-dimensional flat and round spheres, not on S^3.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses geodesic-net classification questions on 2-dimensional spheres, leaving the 3-sphere case unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets on the Round 2-Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geodesic nets on the 2-sphere following Heppes's classification of degree-3 nets.
status_evidence.claim: Classification results are known for the round 2-sphere but not the round 3-sphere.
